title: Figure: An approach to staged exercise prescriptions
source_reference: Ref: (85) - Metkus TS, Baughman KL, Thompson PD. Exercise Prescription and Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease. Circulation 2010; 121(23):2601-2604
actual_image_contents: Flowchart showing staged progression of exercise prescription: walking at conversational pace 5 days per week starting at 10 minutes/session, progressing to 15 minutes/session, then 30 minutes/session, with cardiac symptom checks and strength training (major muscle groups, 8-12 repetitions per set, 2-3 days per week).

nodes.text: Adult patient initiating physical activity / exercise prescription for cardiovascular risk reduction and hypertension control.

nodes.modality: Walking at conversational pace (or enjoyable moderate-intensity activity from Table 2)

nodes.check: Concerning symptoms or repeated exercise intolerance?

nodes.text: Perform cardiac evaluation before continuing or escalating exercise program.

nodes.modality: Walking at conversational pace (accumulated 150 minutes/week moderate activity)
Strength training: major muscle groups (e.g., bicep curls, military press, shrugs, squats, leg curls)
nodes.dosing: One to three sets, 8 to 12 repetitions per set, two to three days per week.

document_name: MoHFW Standard Treatment Guidelines - Hypertension (Quick Reference Guide p.44 & Background Document p.127)
title: Figure 7: Modified World Health Organization (WHO) smoking cessation algorithm
source_reference: Ref: (23) - European guidelines on cardiovascular disease prevention in clinical practice (version 2012) / WHO CVD risk management package
actual_image_contents: Identical flowchart printed in both documents illustrating the 5 As smoking cessation framework: A1: ASK ('Do you use tobacco?'), A2: ADVISE ('Advise to quit in a clear, strong and personalised manner...'), A3: ASSESS ('Are you willing to make a quit attempt now?'), A4: ASSIST ('Assist in preparing a quitting plan: Set quit date, Inform family and friends, Ask for their support, Remove cigarettes/tobacco, Remove objects/articles that prompt smoking, Arrange follow-up visit'), A5: ARRANGE ('At follow-up visit: Congratulate success, reinforce; if relapsed consider more intensive follow-up').
human_review_directive: Do not index for retrieval until human verification against page image is complete.

nodes.text: Reinforce message that tobacco increases risk of heart disease; congratulate non-use.

nodes.script: Advise to quit in a clear, strong and personalised manner: 'Tobacco use increases the risk of developing a heart attack and/or stroke. Quitting tobacco use is the one most important thing you can do to protect your heart and health, you have to quit now.'

nodes.question: Are you willing to make a quit attempt now?

nodes.text: Provide information on health hazards of tobacco and give educational leaflet to the patient. Re-assess readiness at subsequent visits.

plan_components: Remove objects/articles that prompt you to smoke

nodes.schedule: Arrange follow-up visit. Ideally second follow-up visit is recommended within the same month and every month thereafter for 4 months and evaluation after one year. If not feasible, reinforce counselling whenever the patient is seen for blood pressure monitoring.
follow_up_actions: If patient has relapsed, consider more intensive follow-up and support from family

title: Formulary Renal Impairment Advisory Note (Not a Flowchart)
source_reference: MoHFW STG Quick Reference Guide Page 52 (Formulary Annexure)
actual_image_contents: The image on page 52 is NOT a flowchart diagram. It contains a single cautionary statement on renal impairment with standard header and footer: 'Renal impairment: Avoid if creatinine clearance is less than <30 ml/min (approximate serum creatinine 3 mg/dl), when they may be ineffective.' The body of the page is white space resulting from layout formatting following the thiazide formulary section on page 51.
